chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The virgins (daughters) of the fathers are not married off except with the permission of their fathers.

key_terms.ذَوَاتُ الْأَبَّاءِ: The daughters of the fathers (virgin daughters)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for marrying off a virgin daughter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar establishes the necessity of the father's explicit consent (idhn) for the marriage of a virgin (bakarah), a ruling central to Shia jurisprudence regarding wali authority. While the father holds primary authority, scholars distinguish this 'permission' from the 'consent' (riḍā) of the bride, emphasizing that her agreement remains a prerequisite for the validity of the contract. This ruling underscores the balance between paternal guardianship and the daughter's agency in marital arrangements.
